overview: The Invisible Hand is a providence-class dreadnought whose service history spans Clone Wars (22–19 BBY). General Grievous's flagship during the Clone Wars, where Chancellor Palpatine was rescued in the Battle of Coruscant. Imperial archives, Rebel intelligence briefings, and Mandalorian shipyard records estimate total production at ~120 Providence-class hulls, though wartime losses and black-market refits make exact counts difficult to verify.
history:
Design bureaus first drafted the Invisible Hand during the political tensions that defined Clone Wars (22–19 BBY). Engineers prioritised capabilities suited to its role as a providence-class dreadnought, balancing armour, manoeuvrability, and crew requirements against the industrial capacity of the factions that ordered it into production.

As fleet doctrine evolved, the Invisible Hand entered front-line service in convoy escort, planetary assault, and deep-space patrol missions. General Grievous's flagship during the Clone Wars, where Chancellor Palpatine was rescued in the Battle of Coruscant. Veterans praised its reliability under fire while analysts debated whether mass production at ~120 Providence-class hulls diluted quality control across shipyard lines.

Major campaigns cemented the vessel's reputation — whether as a terror weapon, a rebel lifeline, or a smuggler's last hope. Battle damage reports show the providence-class dreadnought could absorb punishment that would destroy lighter craft, though attrition rates climbed sharply during the bloodiest years of galactic war.

In the modern era, surviving hulls appear in private collections, museum orbits, and covert fleets. Restorers hunt spare parts across scrap worlds while historians argue the Invisible Hand symbolises the industrial scale of conflict more than any single battle honour.
significance:
The Invisible Hand illustrates how shipwright traditions and wartime desperation combine to shape galactic warfare. Its providence-class dreadnought layout influenced successor designs long after production lines fell silent.

Approximately ~120 Providence-class hulls hulls served during Clone Wars (22–19 BBY), making the class one of the most visible symbols of its faction's naval power. Colour markings and unit insignia turned anonymous factory output into icons recognised across holonet broadcasts.

For engineers and tacticians, the Invisible Hand remains a case study in trade-offs between firepower, crew survival, and maintenance — lessons still taught at academies from Coruscant to Mandalore.
